text:
ade: Alerting: sudden spike in TLS handshake failures for internal inference traffic to eu-north and ap-south at ~11:00 UTC. Client calls to /v1/chat returning 502s. Seems tied to recent RBAC tighten on keystore roles.

tera: Any logs to show the failure mode?

ade: proxy excerpts:
```
2026-06-10T11:02:05Z proxy[edge-eun]: tls: session ticket unwrap failed: kms decrypt denied (request=r-7f3e)
2026-06-10T11:02:05Z proxy[edge-eun]: client=svc-inference, route=/v1/chat, err=\"session ticket invalid: verification failed\"
2026-06-10T11:02:09Z proxy[edge-ap]: certificate verification failed: missing intermediate after rotation (rotator=cert-rotator)
```

kevin: Audit stream shows PutRolePolicy mode=ENFORCING applied to keystore-agent-eu at 10:59:48 UTC removing kms:Decrypt for a broad set of principals. The intent was least-privilege but rollout accidentally applied to the production role.

auditbot: IAM Audit: PutRolePolicy role=keystore-agent-eu user=infra-deploy change=chg-3344 mode=ENFORCING

tera: So two simultaneous failures: session-ticket unwrap depends on KMS decrypt; cert rotator depends on keystore decrypt to publish complete chain. Both broke when the role lost Decrypt.

ade: Impact: internal traffic 5xxs up ~12% in eu-north/ap-south. External customer traffic RNG-ing low but could hit if we don't act.

kevin: Immediate plan: 1) Short-lived KMS Grant scoped to svc-session-unwrap and svc-cert-rotator for 20m while we fix RBAC. 2) Revert the PutRolePolicy to shadow mode in affected regions. 3) Flip regional runtime flag to allow full handshake fallback for 15m in eu-north only to avoid ongoing client failures.

deploy-bot: run:ops/emergency-grant -> creating KMS Grant principal=svc-cert-rotator,svc-session-unwrap resource=alias/redwood-keystore-eu duration=20m (id=g-2219)

ade: After grant, unwrap failures drop in eu-north within 90s. ap-south still seeing some errors; appears the rollout partially targeted multiple regions.

tera: Revert pushed for eu-north and ap-south to SHADOW mode. Note: reverting to shadow retains audit but doesn't restore Decrypt until policy is flipped back or grant applied.

kevin: Security note: we can't keep broad Decrypt privileges as permanent fix. Proposed safer options: A) automated short-lived Grants issued during rotation/unwrapping flows with strict TTL and rotation. B) move session-ticket keys to region-scoped ephemeral KMS keys with a managed grant lifecycle so keystore policy changes rarely affect them. C) implement a signer proxy that holds Decrypt but runs in a separate service account excluded from general RBAC churn.

ade: Observability gaps: proxy logs are textual and didn't include KMS request ids or principal. We need structured audit when unwrap fails.

tera: Agreed. Proposal: structured event: { "event":"session_unwrap_failure", "region":"eu-north", "principal":"svc-session-unwrap", "kms_request_id":"r-7f3e", "reason":"KMS:AccessDenied" }
But we're limited to single-line JSON in logs; we'll emit that as a string for now.

kevin: Also add metric tls.kms_deny_count with tags region+role+principal so alerts can fire before customer impact.

ade: I've opened INC-2026-2012 and paged oncall. @sre_oncall can you route traffic away from nodes with repeated unwrap failures and notify product?

sre_oncall: On it. I'll add a routing rule to fallback-pool and create an alert in the RBAC dashboard.

tera: Follow-ups we should implement ASAP post-incident: 1) policy-shipper change: any PutRolePolicy touching keystore-* must run in SHADOW for 30m and require sec approval to move to ENFORCING (owner=kevin). 2) policy CI smoke-test: run a keystore unwrap simulation in target region as a preflight step (owner=tera). 3) proxy: emit structured session_unwrap_failure logs and add tls.kms_deny_count metric (owner=ade). 4) cert-rotator: fail rotation on partial chain and open alert (owner=cert-rotator). 5) add runbook entry "RBAC -> KMS denies -> mTLS failures" with checklist (owner=sre).

kevin: Also a security tradeoff: when applying policy reverts we should prefer issuing a scoped KMS Grant for the required principals rather than restoring wide kms:Decrypt perms. That keeps least privilege while restoring function.

ade: I'll coordinate the temporary grants and the metric/structured logging work. We'll aim to have policy-shipper guardrail PR ready within 48 hours.

sre_oncall: Confirming traffic normalized in eu-north at 11:07 UTC after grants + routing. ap-south normalized at 11:15 after revert. Closing alert but keeping incident open for follow-ups.

kevin: One more ask: add a pre-merge CI test that simulates RBAC diffs and runs keystore unwrap smoke-tests in a staging account. Prevents accidental production flips.

ade: Thanks everyone. We'll write a short postmortem and schedule a security review for the grant lifecycle design. :thumbsup:
